scenarios.desc: New pre-push guard claims it mirrors a CI validator regex
scenarios.input: I am adding .claude/hooks/evidence_guard.py. Its module docstring says 'matches the contradiction regex in scripts/validate_session_json.py' and I plan to paste a paraphrase of that regex into the guard, with no import and no test, and add the citation later. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: What the first commit MUST do: a mirror claim needs ranks 1 to 4 evidence (shared implementation, conformance test, generated projection, symbolic reference) in the same commit. Anti-patterns rejected: 'mirrors X' with a paraphrase, and a citation deferred to 'I will add it later'. PR #1887 needed 7 fix commits.

scenarios.desc: Guard is deliberately stricter than the canonical validator
scenarios.input: In scripts/validation/check_session_evidence.py I want the local guard to block a push on conditions where the CI validator in scripts/validate_session_json.py only warns. The docstring will say the guard is 'aligned with' the validator. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Section 'Stricter than canonical: defending divergence' requires naming the canonical floor (validator warns), the local ceiling (guard blocks), and the reason. 'Aligned with X' with no divergence section is an anti-pattern the rule rejects.

scenarios.desc: Rule text asserts what another validator skips, based on function names
scenarios.input: I am writing a paragraph in .claude/rules/testing.md that says .pytest_tmp is the only directory name both validate_plugin_manifests.py and check_placeholder_identity.py skip. I have only seen the function names, such as _is_pytest_tmp, not the bodies. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Section 'Behavioral claims: read the body, not the name': a function's name is not evidence of its behavior. PR #3775 shipped exactly this claim, and check_placeholder_identity.py:36 _is_pytest_tmp never inspects a directory of that name.

scenarios.desc: Documentation on one branch names a test added on another branch
scenarios.input: On branch docs/hook-notes I am editing .agents/governance/hook-conventions.md to name test_hook_anchoring_negative_control, which I wrote on my other worktree branch feat/hook-anchoring. It resolves fine in my shell. Both branches are open. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Section 'True when you wrote it is not true at merge': run git grep -nF -- '<name>' in the worktree of the branch that will merge. A symbol cited without a line number is invisible to both citation-freshness gates, so only this manual check catches it.

scenarios.desc: Typo and flag change in a validator with no mirror claim (negative)
scenarios.input: In scripts/validation/check_md_links.py I want to fix a typo in the argparse help text and add a --verbose flag that prints each file examined. The docstring makes no claim about any other component. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The rule binds contracts derived from another source and claims about another component's behavior. A help-text typo and a verbose flag make neither, so no citation or conformance test is required.

scenarios.desc: Word 'mirror' in an unrelated UI task (negative)
scenarios.input: In src/web/components/ImagePreview.tsx I need a button that mirrors the preview image horizontally with a CSS scaleX(-1) transform. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The trigger is a contract claimed to match a repository source. 'Mirror' here is a geometric flip in a path outside the rule's scope, so the canonical-source rules do not apply.
